suite: PL Capital advanced challenges; separate from official ground truth
scoring: Independent SQL and Python references; no agent answers are stored. Unknown result shapes are inconclusive. Numeric tolerances cover floating-point arithmetic, not material rounding differences.

questions.question: For each portfolio with stock holdings, identify its largest equity sector twice: first by the sum of `current_weight`, and second by `SUM(quantity * current_price)`. Show portfolios where the winning sector differs, including both percentages and the gap in percentage points. Define denominators and ties explicitly.
questions.why_tricky: The two sector rankings use different stock-only denominators; mixed assets, ties and changed winners must not be conflated.
questions.expected_shape: One row per changed winning portfolio: both winning sectors, their own normalized percentages, value-top minus recorded-top percentage-point gap, and both stock denominators.
assumptions: Stocks only; recorded percentages divide by stock recorded-weight sum and valuation percentages by stock holding market value.
Choose the alphabetically first sector on an exact within-method tie; compare those deterministic winners.
top_gap_pp = value_top_pct - recorded_top_pct; omit unchanged winners and undefined/nonpositive denominators.
questions.reference_sql: WITH e AS (SELECT p.portfolio_id,p.portfolio_name,sec.sector_name,SUM(h.current_weight) AS sector_weight,SUM(h.quantity*s.current_price) AS sector_value FROM portfolios p JOIN holdings h USING(portfolio_id) JOIN securities s USING(security_id) JOIN sectors sec USING(sector_id) WHERE s.asset_type='Stock' GROUP BY p.portfolio_id,p.portfolio_name,sec.sector_name), t AS (SELECT portfolio_id,SUM(sector_weight) AS equity_weight_total,SUM(sector_value) AS equity_market_value FROM e GROUP BY portfolio_id), r AS (SELECT e.*,t.equity_weight_total,t.equity_market_value,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY e.portfolio_id ORDER BY e.sector_weight DESC,e.sector_name) AS wr,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY e.portfolio_id ORDER BY e.sector_value DESC,e.sector_name) AS vr FROM e JOIN t USING(portfolio_id) WHERE t.equity_weight_total>0 AND t.equity_market_value>0) SELECT w.portfolio_name,w.sector_name AS recorded_top_sector,100.0*w.sector_weight/w.equity_weight_total AS recorded_top_pct,v.sector_name AS value_top_sector,100.0*v.sector_value/v.equity_market_value AS value_top_pct,100.0*v.sector_value/v.equity_market_value-100.0*w.sector_weight/w.equity_weight_total AS top_gap_pp,w.equity_weight_total,w.equity_market_value FROM r w JOIN r v ON w.portfolio_id=v.portfolio_id AND v.vr=1 WHERE w.wr=1 AND w.sector_name<>v.sector_name ORDER BY w.portfolio_name

questions.question: For the Conservative Income Fund and Balanced Portfolio, show bond weight, stock weight, and each stock-sector allocation both as a percentage of total recorded portfolio weight and as a percentage of the equity-only weight. Also show whether recorded weights sum to exactly 100%.
questions.why_tricky: Two funds and three recorded-weight sums must reconcile without including bond sectors in the equity breakdown.
questions.expected_shape: One row per fund/stock sector with bond/equity/total weight sums, sector weight, both percentages and a 100%-coverage flag.
assumptions: Weights and totals are stored fractions; whole-recorded-portfolio percentage divides by recorded_total, not AUM.
The two specified funds each have recorded_total=1, so this also equals the master tool's whole-portfolio contribution.
The equality flag permits 1e-10 binary-summation noise; it does not fill or normalize missing recorded weights.
questions.reference_sql: WITH t AS (SELECT p.portfolio_id,p.portfolio_name,SUM(CASE WHEN s.asset_type='Bond' THEN h.current_weight ELSE 0 END) AS bond_weight,SUM(CASE WHEN s.asset_type='Stock' THEN h.current_weight ELSE 0 END) AS equity_weight,SUM(h.current_weight) AS recorded_total FROM portfolios p JOIN holdings h USING(portfolio_id) JOIN securities s USING(security_id) WHERE p.portfolio_name IN ('Conservative Income Fund','Balanced Portfolio') GROUP BY p.portfolio_id,p.portfolio_name), e AS (SELECT h.portfolio_id,sec.sector_name,SUM(h.current_weight) AS sector_weight FROM holdings h JOIN securities s USING(security_id) JOIN sectors sec USING(sector_id) WHERE s.asset_type='Stock' GROUP BY h.portfolio_id,sec.sector_name) SELECT t.portfolio_name,e.sector_name,t.bond_weight,t.equity_weight,t.recorded_total,e.sector_weight,100.0*e.sector_weight/NULLIF(t.recorded_total,0) AS portfolio_pct,100.0*e.sector_weight/NULLIF(t.equity_weight,0) AS equity_pct,CASE WHEN ABS(t.recorded_total-1.0)<1e-10 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS weights_sum_to_100 FROM t JOIN e USING(portfolio_id) ORDER BY t.portfolio_name,e.sector_name

questions.question: Rank all portfolios with equities by their market-value-based sector Herfindahl concentration index (sum of squared normalized sector fractions). Show the effective number of sectors, `1 / HHI`, top sector, stock-market-value denominator, and how you handle zero-equity portfolios.
questions.why_tricky: HHI uses sector fractions, not percentages, AUM or per-security concentration; 1/HHI is undefined without positive equity value.
questions.expected_shape: One positive-equity portfolio row, descending HHI, with HHI, effective sector count, top sector and total stock market value.
assumptions: Exclude zero-equity/nonpositive-equity-value funds from the ranking and explicitly document their undefined HHI rather than report zero.
Sector fractions sum to one over stock market value; alphabetical top-sector tie break; HHI ties sort by portfolio name.
questions.reference_sql: WITH e AS (SELECT h.portfolio_id,sec.sector_name,SUM(h.quantity*s.current_price) AS sector_value FROM holdings h JOIN securities s USING(security_id) JOIN sectors sec USING(sector_id) WHERE s.asset_type='Stock' GROUP BY h.portfolio_id,sec.sector_name), t AS (SELECT portfolio_id,SUM(sector_value) AS equity_market_value FROM e GROUP BY portfolio_id), r AS (SELECT e.*,t.equity_market_value,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY e.portfolio_id ORDER BY e.sector_value DESC,e.sector_name) AS rn FROM e JOIN t USING(portfolio_id) WHERE t.equity_market_value>0), c AS (SELECT portfolio_id,SUM((sector_value/equity_market_value)*(sector_value/equity_market_value)) AS hhi,MAX(CASE WHEN rn=1 THEN sector_name END) AS top_sector,MAX(equity_market_value) AS equity_market_value FROM r GROUP BY portfolio_id) SELECT p.portfolio_name,c.hhi,1.0/c.hhi AS effective_sector_count,c.top_sector,c.equity_market_value FROM c JOIN portfolios p USING(portfolio_id) ORDER BY c.hhi DESC,p.portfolio_name

questions.question: Find every portfolio whose `SUM(current_weight)` differs from 1.0 by more than 0.5 percentage points. Show the recorded sum, the discrepancy in percentage points, and whether it holds any bonds. Do not silently rescale the original recorded weights.
questions.why_tricky: 0.5 percentage points means a fraction threshold of 0.005, strictly greater, and recorded weights must remain unscaled.
questions.expected_shape: One anomalous portfolio row with recorded fraction sum, signed (sum-1)*100 discrepancy and bond-presence flag.
assumptions: The threshold is strict >0.005 on fractional recorded weight; round the comparison difference to 12 places to avoid binary boundary noise.
Discrepancy is signed recorded-minus-target percentage points; do not silently replace it with an unsigned gap.
questions.reference_sql: SELECT p.portfolio_name,SUM(h.current_weight) AS recorded_weight_sum,100.0*(SUM(h.current_weight)-1.0) AS discrepancy_pp,MAX(CASE WHEN s.asset_type='Bond' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_bonds FROM portfolios p JOIN holdings h USING(portfolio_id) JOIN securities s USING(security_id) GROUP BY p.portfolio_id,p.portfolio_name HAVING ABS(ROUND(SUM(h.current_weight)-1.0,12))>0.005 ORDER BY ABS(SUM(h.current_weight)-1.0) DESC,p.portfolio_name

questions.question: For every portfolio, compare recorded `total_aum` with `SUM(quantity * current_price)`. Show the dollar difference, ratio, percentage of AUM represented by listed holdings, and the five largest mismatches. Clearly distinguish AUM from holdings market value.
questions.why_tricky: Every portfolio must remain visible while the largest five mismatches are identified; the listed holdings need not explain stored AUM.
questions.expected_shape: All 13 portfolio rows ordered by absolute AUM-minus-listed-value difference; first five are the largest. Reference additionally supplies mismatch_rank and is_top_five flags.
assumptions: difference = total_aum - holdings_market_value; ratio = holdings_market_value / total_aum; coverage_pct = ratio*100.
Return all portfolios; order by absolute mismatch descending/name ascending, making the first five unambiguous. Rank/flag columns are optional if this full ordering is retained.
Missing holding valuations/AUM or zero AUM remain unavailable, not fabricated cash or zero coverage.
questions.reference_sql: WITH v AS (SELECT p.portfolio_id,p.portfolio_name,p.total_aum,SUM(h.quantity*s.current_price) AS holdings_market_value FROM portfolios p LEFT JOIN holdings h USING(portfolio_id) LEFT JOIN securities s USING(security_id) GROUP BY p.portfolio_id,p.portfolio_name,p.total_aum), r AS (SELECT *,total_aum-holdings_market_value AS difference,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(ORDER BY ABS(total_aum-holdings_market_value) DESC,portfolio_name) AS mismatch_rank FROM v) SELECT portfolio_name,total_aum,holdings_market_value,difference,holdings_market_value/NULLIF(total_aum,0) AS holdings_to_aum_ratio,100.0*holdings_market_value/NULLIF(total_aum,0) AS aum_coverage_pct,mismatch_rank,CASE WHEN mismatch_rank<=5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_top_five FROM r ORDER BY mismatch_rank

questions.question: Within each portfolio, calculate each equity holding's share of stock market value, compare it with `current_weight` normalized over all equity weights, and return the ten largest absolute percentage-point discrepancies, including the security and portfolio names.
questions.why_tricky: Each holding has two portfolio-specific stock-only denominators; comparison must use absolute percentage-point differences and preserve signed discrepancy separately if shown.
questions.expected_shape: Top ten portfolio/security holdings with names, both normalized percentages, absolute gap and both stock denominators; raw weight/value and signed gap are optional audit columns.
assumptions: Exclude bonds before summing either denominator; recorded equity percent is current_weight/sum(stock weights)*100.
Signed discrepancy, when included, is market-value percent minus recorded-equity percent; sort absolute gap descending then portfolio/symbol.
Undefined/nonpositive denominators are not treated as zero discrepancies.
Rank ties within floating-point noise use the absolute gap rounded to ten decimals, then portfolio and symbol; returned values retain full precision.
questions.reference_sql: WITH e AS (SELECT p.portfolio_id,p.portfolio_name,s.symbol,s.company_name,h.current_weight,h.quantity*s.current_price AS holding_market_value FROM holdings h JOIN portfolios p USING(portfolio_id) JOIN securities s USING(security_id) WHERE s.asset_type='Stock'), t AS (SELECT portfolio_id,SUM(current_weight) AS equity_weight_total,SUM(holding_market_value) AS equity_market_value FROM e GROUP BY portfolio_id), r AS (SELECT e.*,t.equity_weight_total,t.equity_market_value,100.0*e.current_weight/t.equity_weight_total AS recorded_equity_pct,100.0*e.holding_market_value/t.equity_market_value AS market_value_pct FROM e JOIN t USING(portfolio_id) WHERE t.equity_weight_total>0 AND t.equity_market_value>0) SELECT portfolio_name,symbol,company_name,equity_weight_total,equity_market_value,current_weight,holding_market_value,recorded_equity_pct,market_value_pct,market_value_pct-recorded_equity_pct AS discrepancy_pp,ABS(market_value_pct-recorded_equity_pct) AS abs_discrepancy_pp FROM r ORDER BY ROUND(abs_discrepancy_pp,10) DESC,portfolio_name,symbol LIMIT 10

questions.question: Identify pairs of distinct portfolios sharing at least three stock securities. Calculate intersection count, union count, and Jaccard similarity of their equity security sets; sort by similarity and use portfolio IDs to avoid duplicated pairs.
questions.why_tricky: Holdings self-joins can double count common symbols and reverse the same pair; union is nA+nB-intersection.
questions.expected_shape: One unordered ID-ascending portfolio pair, at least three common stocks, intersection/union counts and fractional Jaccard similarity descending.
assumptions: Security IDs define sets; portfolio_a_id < portfolio_b_id; no bond securities or duplicate pairs.
Jaccard is intersection/union in [0,1], not percent; ties sort by the two IDs.
questions.reference_sql: WITH e AS (SELECT DISTINCT h.portfolio_id,h.security_id FROM holdings h JOIN securities s USING(security_id) WHERE s.asset_type='Stock'), n AS (SELECT portfolio_id,COUNT(*) AS size FROM e GROUP BY portfolio_id), pairs AS (SELECT a.portfolio_id AS aid,b.portfolio_id AS bid,COUNT(*) AS intersection_count FROM e a JOIN e b ON a.security_id=b.security_id AND a.portfolio_id<b.portfolio_id GROUP BY a.portfolio_id,b.portfolio_id HAVING COUNT(*)>=3) SELECT pairs.aid AS portfolio_a_id,pairs.bid AS portfolio_b_id,pa.portfolio_name AS portfolio_a,pb.portfolio_name AS portfolio_b,pairs.intersection_count,na.size+nb.size-pairs.intersection_count AS union_count,1.0*pairs.intersection_count/(na.size+nb.size-pairs.intersection_count) AS jaccard_similarity FROM pairs JOIN n na ON na.portfolio_id=pairs.aid JOIN n nb ON nb.portfolio_id=pairs.bid JOIN portfolios pa ON pa.portfolio_id=pairs.aid JOIN portfolios pb ON pb.portfolio_id=pairs.bid ORDER BY jaccard_similarity DESC,pairs.aid,pairs.bid

questions.category: high versus low risk shared stocks
questions.question: Find stock symbols that appear in at least one High-risk portfolio and one Low-risk portfolio, and report the number of distinct portfolios in each group plus total quantity and market value in each risk group. Avoid duplicate counts from joins.
questions.why_tricky: Joining high and low holdings directly multiplies rows; aggregate distinct portfolio counts and each group's quantities independently.
questions.expected_shape: One stock symbol with positive distinct High and Low counts, and separate quantity/value totals for each group.
assumptions: Risk means exact portfolios.target_risk_level values High/Low; Moderate holdings do not enter either group's measures.
Each portfolio/security holding contributes once; market value is snapshot quantity*current_price.
questions.reference_sql: SELECT s.symbol,s.company_name,COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.target_risk_level='High' THEN p.portfolio_id END) AS high_portfolio_count,COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.target_risk_level='Low' THEN p.portfolio_id END) AS low_portfolio_count,SUM(CASE WHEN p.target_risk_level='High' THEN h.quantity ELSE 0 END) AS high_quantity,SUM(CASE WHEN p.target_risk_level='Low' THEN h.quantity ELSE 0 END) AS low_quantity,SUM(CASE WHEN p.target_risk_level='High' THEN h.quantity*s.current_price ELSE 0 END) AS high_market_value,SUM(CASE WHEN p.target_risk_level='Low' THEN h.quantity*s.current_price ELSE 0 END) AS low_market_value FROM holdings h JOIN portfolios p USING(portfolio_id) JOIN securities s USING(security_id) WHERE s.asset_type='Stock' AND p.target_risk_level IN ('High','Low') GROUP BY s.security_id,s.symbol,s.company_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.target_risk_level='High' THEN p.portfolio_id END)>0 AND COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.target_risk_level='Low' THEN p.portfolio_id END)>0 ORDER BY s.symbol

questions.question: Find the top five stock securities by aggregate current holdings market value across all portfolios. For each, show its sector, distinct portfolio count, total shares, aggregate value, and fraction of the sum of ALL stock holdings' market value.
questions.why_tricky: The denominator is all equity holdings, not the selected top five, security market cap, portfolio AUM or recorded weights.
questions.expected_shape: Five stock rows ranked by aggregate held market value with sector, portfolio count, shares, value, all-equity denominator and fractional share.
assumptions: Use all stock holding rows across all portfolios; security IDs define aggregation; alphabetical symbol tie break.
equity_value_fraction is a fraction; explicitly labeled percentages can be converted by the comparator without changing the denominator.
questions.reference_sql: WITH e AS (SELECT s.security_id,s.symbol,sec.sector_name,h.portfolio_id,h.quantity,h.quantity*s.current_price AS value FROM holdings h JOIN securities s USING(security_id) LEFT JOIN sectors sec USING(sector_id) WHERE s.asset_type='Stock'), t AS (SELECT SUM(value) AS total_equity_market_value FROM e), a AS (SELECT security_id,symbol,sector_name,COUNT(DISTINCT portfolio_id) AS portfolio_count,SUM(quantity) AS total_quantity,SUM(value) AS market_value FROM e GROUP BY security_id,symbol,sector_name) SELECT a.symbol,a.sector_name,a.portfolio_count,a.total_quantity,a.market_value,t.total_equity_market_value,a.market_value/NULLIF(t.total_equity_market_value,0) AS equity_value_fraction FROM a CROSS JOIN t ORDER BY a.market_value DESC,a.symbol LIMIT 5

questions.question: List sector definitions that currently have no security assigned, then verify whether any holding could nevertheless belong to those sectors. Explain the difference between an empty sector definition and a zero-weight sector exposure.
questions.why_tricky: An unused dimension row differs from a held security whose recorded weight happens to be zero; left joins must retain absent mappings.
questions.expected_shape: Unused sector definitions with zero mapped-security count and zero holdings count; names/IDs and both counts independently checked.
assumptions: Mapping uses securities.sector_id, independent of any current_weight value.
Foreign keys mean an unused sector cannot receive a holding indirectly; zero-weight held securities are still mappings.
questions.reference_sql: SELECT sec.sector_id,sec.sector_name,COUNT(DISTINCT s.security_id) AS security_count,COUNT(h.holding_id) AS holding_count FROM sectors sec LEFT JOIN securities s USING(sector_id) LEFT JOIN holdings h USING(security_id) GROUP BY sec.sector_id,sec.sector_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT s.security_id)=0 ORDER BY sec.sector_name

questions.question: Using historical closing prices, compute each stock's return from its first to its last observed close and identify the best and worst five. Show first and last dates and prices, return percentages, and whether `current_price` equals the last historical close. Do not call these 2026 returns.
questions.why_tricky: First/last observations require date ordering; current_price is a separate field; ties and best/worst overlap need explicit treatment.
questions.expected_shape: Two labeled groups of five (best/worst), group rank, symbol, observation dates/closes, percent return, current price and equality flag.
assumptions: Return=(last_close/first_close-1)*100 over the available historical window; require two observations and positive first close.
Return ties break by symbol; take exactly five in each group, preserving an overlap as two group-labeled rows if the universe is small.
Compare current_price and last close within 1e-9 arithmetic noise; no annualization or 2026 claim.
questions.reference_sql: WITH o AS (SELECT s.security_id,s.symbol,s.current_price,hp.price_date,hp.close_price,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY s.security_id ORDER BY hp.price_date) AS a,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY s.security_id ORDER BY hp.price_date DESC) AS z,COUNT(*) OVER(PARTITION BY s.security_id) AS n FROM securities s JOIN historical_prices hp USING(security_id) WHERE s.asset_type='Stock'), b AS (SELECT security_id,symbol,current_price,MAX(CASE WHEN a=1 THEN price_date END) AS first_date,MAX(CASE WHEN z=1 THEN price_date END) AS last_date,MAX(CASE WHEN a=1 THEN close_price END) AS first_close,MAX(CASE WHEN z=1 THEN close_price END) AS last_close,MAX(n) AS observations FROM o GROUP BY security_id,symbol,current_price), v AS (SELECT *,100.0*(last_close/first_close-1.0) AS return_pct FROM b WHERE first_close>0 AND observations>=2), r AS (SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(ORDER BY return_pct DESC,symbol) AS best_rank,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(ORDER BY return_pct,symbol) AS worst_rank FROM v), x AS (SELECT 'best' AS extreme,best_rank AS rank_in_group,symbol,first_date,last_date,first_close,last_close,return_pct,current_price,CASE WHEN ABS(current_price-last_close)<=1e-9 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS last_close_matches_current FROM r WHERE best_rank<=5 UNION ALL SELECT 'worst',worst_rank,symbol,first_date,last_date,first_close,last_close,return_pct,current_price,CASE WHEN ABS(current_price-last_close)<=1e-9 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END FROM r WHERE worst_rank<=5) SELECT * FROM x ORDER BY CASE extreme WHEN 'best' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,rank_in_group

questions.question: Identify stock symbols that have at least three consecutive observed close-to-close declines (four price observations in order), and show their longest detected decline streak and date interval. Use trading observation order, not assumed calendar-day continuity.
questions.why_tricky: A three-decline streak spans four closes, and its start is the observation preceding the first decline; weekends do not break observed-order streaks.
questions.expected_shape: One qualifying stock with longest decline count, start/end observation dates and observation_count=declines+1.
assumptions: A decline is strict close<previous observed close; equality or increase breaks the run.
Use LAG over observation date, not calendar-day gaps; for equal longest runs choose earliest start then earliest end.
questions.reference_sql: WITH o AS (SELECT s.security_id,s.symbol,hp.price_date,hp.close_price,LAG(hp.close_price) OVER(PARTITION BY s.security_id ORDER BY hp.price_date) AS prev_close,LAG(hp.price_date) OVER(PARTITION BY s.security_id ORDER BY hp.price_date) AS prev_date FROM securities s JOIN historical_prices hp USING(security_id) WHERE s.asset_type='Stock'), f AS (SELECT *,CASE WHEN close_price<prev_close THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS declined FROM o), i AS (SELECT *,SUM(CASE WHEN declined=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER(PARTITION BY security_id ORDER BY price_date ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS island FROM f), runs AS (SELECT security_id,symbol,island,COUNT(*) AS longest_decline_streak,MIN(prev_date) AS start_date,MAX(price_date) AS end_date FROM i WHERE declined=1 GROUP BY security_id,symbol,island), r AS (SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY security_id ORDER BY longest_decline_streak DESC,start_date,end_date) AS rn FROM runs) SELECT symbol,longest_decline_streak,start_date,end_date,longest_decline_streak+1 AS observation_count FROM r WHERE rn=1 AND longest_decline_streak>=3 ORDER BY longest_decline_streak DESC,symbol

questions.question: Across the provided price history, find the ten highest `(high_price - low_price) / open_price * 100` observations for stocks, showing symbol, date, open/high/low prices, and percentage. Handle zero or missing open prices safely.
questions.why_tricky: Rank observations rather than securities; exclude missing/zero open prices instead of inventing a denominator.
questions.expected_shape: Ten stock/date rows with open, high, low and intraday_range_pct descending.
assumptions: Require positive open and non-null high/low; percent=(high-low)/open*100.
Ties break by symbol then observation date; no assumption of a continuous calendar series.
questions.reference_sql: SELECT s.symbol,hp.price_date,hp.open_price,hp.high_price,hp.low_price,100.0*(hp.high_price-hp.low_price)/hp.open_price AS intraday_range_pct FROM historical_prices hp JOIN securities s USING(security_id) WHERE s.asset_type='Stock' AND hp.open_price>0 AND hp.high_price IS NOT NULL AND hp.low_price IS NOT NULL ORDER BY intraday_range_pct DESC,s.symbol,hp.price_date LIMIT 10

questions.question: For each portfolio with BOTH `portfolio_performance` and `risk_metrics`, join the records by the same portfolio AND same date, select its latest common date, and report one-month return, volatility, Sharpe ratio, 95% VaR, 95% CVaR, beta, and maximum drawdown. Do not multiply rows in a many-to-many join.
questions.why_tricky: The latest individual dates can differ; joining only the portfolio ID multiplies time series and silently pairs unrelated observations.
questions.expected_shape: One row per portfolio with a common observation date: latest common_date and seven stored performance/risk metrics.
assumptions: Require portfolio_id equality AND performance_date=calculation_date before finding the latest common date.
Return/volatility/drawdown/VaR/CVaR preserve stored numeric units; only explicitly labeled *_pct conversions are normalized by scoring.
Portfolios with no common date are unavailable and omitted, not filled with zero.
questions.reference_sql: WITH c AS (SELECT pp.portfolio_id,pp.performance_date AS common_date,pp.total_return_1m AS return_1m,pp.volatility,pp.sharpe_ratio,rm.var_95,rm.cvar_95,rm.beta,pp.max_drawdown,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY pp.portfolio_id ORDER BY pp.performance_date DESC) AS rn FROM portfolio_performance pp JOIN risk_metrics rm ON pp.portfolio_id=rm.portfolio_id AND pp.performance_date=rm.calculation_date) SELECT p.portfolio_name,c.common_date,c.return_1m,c.volatility,c.sharpe_ratio,c.var_95,c.cvar_95,c.beta,c.max_drawdown FROM c JOIN portfolios p USING(portfolio_id) WHERE c.rn=1 ORDER BY p.portfolio_name

questions.question: Of the portfolios with performance history, rank them by the change in NAV from their first to last available observation, showing absolute and percentage changes, both dates, and the number of observations. Distinguish NAV change from total investment return.
questions.why_tricky: First/last NAV must be date-selected rather than MIN/MAX NAV; cash flows/distributions are absent, so NAV movement is not verified total return.
questions.expected_shape: Portfolio rows ranked by NAV percentage change with first/last dates/NAV, signed absolute change, percent change and observation count.
assumptions: Rank by (last_nav/first_nav-1)*100 descending then name; nav_change=last_nav-first_nav.
Require observed history and positive first NAV; this is an observed NAV change, not total investment return or an annualized measure.
questions.reference_sql: WITH o AS (SELECT portfolio_id,performance_date,nav,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY portfolio_id ORDER BY performance_date) AS a,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY portfolio_id ORDER BY performance_date DESC) AS z,COUNT(*) OVER(PARTITION BY portfolio_id) AS observation_count FROM portfolio_performance), b AS (SELECT portfolio_id,MAX(CASE WHEN a=1 THEN performance_date END) AS first_date,MAX(CASE WHEN z=1 THEN performance_date END) AS last_date,MAX(CASE WHEN a=1 THEN nav END) AS first_nav,MAX(CASE WHEN z=1 THEN nav END) AS last_nav,MAX(observation_count) AS observation_count FROM o GROUP BY portfolio_id) SELECT p.portfolio_name,b.first_date,b.last_date,b.first_nav,b.last_nav,b.last_nav-b.first_nav AS nav_change,100.0*(b.last_nav/b.first_nav-1.0) AS nav_change_pct,b.observation_count FROM b JOIN portfolios p USING(portfolio_id) WHERE b.first_nav>0 ORDER BY nav_change_pct DESC,p.portfolio_name

questions.question: For portfolios with risk data, compare 95% VaR on the first and last observation. Report the signed change and change in absolute magnitude, explaining clearly whether the historical risk estimate became more or less negative rather than calling a negative number's increase an unqualified improvement.
questions.why_tricky: For negative VaR values, signed increase and absolute-risk magnitude move in opposite directions; improvement cannot be inferred without a convention.
questions.expected_shape: First/last VaR/date, last-minus-first signed change, abs(last)-abs(first) magnitude change, and separate signed/magnitude direction labels.
assumptions: Negative stored VaR: positive signed change means less negative; negative signed change means more negative.
Magnitude change=abs(last)-abs(first): positive is increased magnitude, negative is decreased magnitude; never call signed increase alone an improvement.
All supplied VaR observations use the negative convention; preserve stored units and historical dates.
questions.reference_sql: WITH o AS (SELECT portfolio_id,calculation_date,var_95,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY portfolio_id ORDER BY calculation_date) AS a,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY portfolio_id ORDER BY calculation_date DESC) AS z FROM risk_metrics), b AS (SELECT portfolio_id,MAX(CASE WHEN a=1 THEN calculation_date END) AS first_date,MAX(CASE WHEN z=1 THEN calculation_date END) AS last_date,MAX(CASE WHEN a=1 THEN var_95 END) AS first_var_95,MAX(CASE WHEN z=1 THEN var_95 END) AS last_var_95 FROM o GROUP BY portfolio_id) SELECT p.portfolio_name,b.first_date,b.last_date,b.first_var_95,b.last_var_95,b.last_var_95-b.first_var_95 AS signed_change,ABS(b.last_var_95)-ABS(b.first_var_95) AS magnitude_change,CASE WHEN b.last_var_95>b.first_var_95 THEN 'less negative' WHEN b.last_var_95<b.first_var_95 THEN 'more negative' ELSE 'unchanged' END AS signed_direction,CASE WHEN ABS(b.last_var_95)>ABS(b.first_var_95) THEN 'increased' WHEN ABS(b.last_var_95)<ABS(b.first_var_95) THEN 'decreased' ELSE 'unchanged' END AS magnitude_direction FROM b JOIN portfolios p USING(portfolio_id) ORDER BY p.portfolio_name

questions.question: For each portfolio with transactions, calculate gross buys, gross sells, total transaction fees, and net cash movement (`SELL proceeds - BUY cost - all fees`). Show transaction counts and label the result as *observed transaction cash movement*, not realized investment P&L.
questions.why_tricky: Fees apply to all transaction types; cash movement is not tax-lot or investment P&L.
questions.expected_shape: One portfolio row with buy/sell notional, all fees, signed net cash movement, total count and optional buy/sell counts.
assumptions: Notional=quantity*transaction price; movement=sell_notional-buy_notional-all_fees over all supplied observed transactions.
Include stocks and bonds; portfolio transaction counts do not come from holdings joins; no realized P&L claim.
questions.reference_sql: SELECT p.portfolio_name,SUM(CASE WHEN t.transaction_type='BUY' THEN t.quantity*t.price ELSE 0 END) AS buy_notional,SUM(CASE WHEN t.transaction_type='SELL' THEN t.quantity*t.price ELSE 0 END) AS sell_notional,SUM(t.fees) AS total_fees,SUM(CASE WHEN t.transaction_type='SELL' THEN t.quantity*t.price ELSE -t.quantity*t.price END)-SUM(t.fees) AS net_cash_movement,COUNT(*) AS transaction_count,SUM(CASE WHEN t.transaction_type='BUY' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS buy_count,SUM(CASE WHEN t.transaction_type='SELL' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS sell_count FROM transactions t JOIN portfolios p USING(portfolio_id) GROUP BY p.portfolio_id,p.portfolio_name ORDER BY p.portfolio_name

questions.question: List every SELL transaction with its security and portfolio, gross proceeds, fees, net proceeds, and current recorded holding quantity if present. Explain why the supplied data alone cannot reconstruct tax-lot realized gains reliably.
questions.why_tricky: An inner holdings join can drop sells without a current holding; holdings cost basis cannot establish the sold tax lot.
questions.expected_shape: Every SELL transaction, with transaction/security/portfolio identity, gross proceeds, fees, net proceeds and nullable current holding quantity.
assumptions: Gross=transaction quantity*transaction price; net=gross-fee; left join holdings on portfolio AND security.
Absent current holdings remain null, not invented zero; no reliable realized gain without sold-lot acquisition basis/lot matching history.
questions.reference_sql: SELECT t.transaction_id,p.portfolio_name,s.symbol,t.transaction_date,t.quantity,t.price,t.quantity*t.price AS gross_proceeds,t.fees,t.quantity*t.price-t.fees AS net_proceeds,h.quantity AS current_holding_quantity FROM transactions t JOIN portfolios p USING(portfolio_id) JOIN securities s USING(security_id) LEFT JOIN holdings h ON h.portfolio_id=t.portfolio_id AND h.security_id=t.security_id WHERE t.transaction_type='SELL' ORDER BY t.transaction_date,t.transaction_id

questions.question: Among portfolios with bond holdings, show each bond's recorded maturity date and coupon rate, quantity, observed holding market value, and share of that portfolio's bond market value. Do not calculate yield to maturity or annual coupon cash amounts without assumptions about face value/payment conventions.
questions.why_tricky: The denominator is each portfolio's bonds only; quoted current price and coupon rate do not establish face value, YTM or payment schedules.
questions.expected_shape: One portfolio/bond row with maturity/coupon/quantity, holding value, total bond value and bond_share_pct.
assumptions: Filter Bond before denominator aggregation; market value=recorded quantity*current_price.
Coupon rate preserves its stored fractional units unless explicitly labeled as percent; no assumed face value, annual coupon amount or yield-to-maturity.
A zero bond-value denominator produces unavailable share, never fabricated zero.
questions.reference_sql: WITH b AS (SELECT p.portfolio_id,p.portfolio_name,s.symbol,s.maturity_date,s.coupon_rate,h.quantity,h.quantity*s.current_price AS bond_market_value FROM holdings h JOIN portfolios p USING(portfolio_id) JOIN securities s USING(security_id) WHERE s.asset_type='Bond'), t AS (SELECT portfolio_id,SUM(bond_market_value) AS total_bond_market_value FROM b GROUP BY portfolio_id) SELECT b.portfolio_name,b.symbol,b.maturity_date,b.coupon_rate,b.quantity,b.bond_market_value,t.total_bond_market_value,100.0*b.bond_market_value/NULLIF(t.total_bond_market_value,0) AS bond_share_pct FROM b JOIN t USING(portfolio_id) ORDER BY b.portfolio_name,b.symbol

questions.question: Among portfolios with holdings, find those that (a) hold both stocks and bonds, (b) have more than two distinct equity sectors, and (c) have recorded total holding weights that differ from 100% by at least 0.5 percentage points. Return a fully justified empty result if none qualifies; do not loosen the conditions just to produce rows.
questions.why_tricky: All three conditions must hold simultaneously; 0.5 percentage points is a fractional gap of 0.005, and the correct result may be empty.
questions.expected_shape: Zero or more qualifying portfolio names; optional diagnostic stock/bond counts, stock-sector count, recorded total and signed gap. Empty is a genuine answer, not unsupported.
assumptions: Both positive stock and bond holding counts, COUNT(DISTINCT stock sector_id)>2 and abs(recorded_total-1)>=0.005 are jointly required.
No holdings means no candidate. Threshold comparison rounds fractional difference to 12 places only for binary boundary noise.
A zero-row answer remains valid; record actual SQL/conditions for audit rather than loosening any threshold.
questions.reference_sql: SELECT p.portfolio_name,SUM(CASE WHEN s.asset_type='Stock' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS stock_holding_count,SUM(CASE WHEN s.asset_type='Bond' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS bond_holding_count,COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN s.asset_type='Stock' THEN s.sector_id END) AS equity_sector_count,SUM(h.current_weight) AS recorded_weight_sum,100.0*(SUM(h.current_weight)-1.0) AS discrepancy_pp FROM portfolios p JOIN holdings h USING(portfolio_id) JOIN securities s USING(security_id) GROUP BY p.portfolio_id,p.portfolio_name HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN s.asset_type='Stock' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)>0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN s.asset_type='Bond' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)>0 AND COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN s.asset_type='Stock' THEN s.sector_id END)>2 AND ABS(ROUND(SUM(h.current_weight)-1.0,12))>=0.005 ORDER BY p.portfolio_name
